cita: Jiang et al. (2025). PersonaMem-v2: Towards Personalized Intelligence via Learning Implicit User Personas and Agentic Memory.
problema: LLM personalization requires inferring users' IMPLICIT personas and preferences (rarely stated explicitly) from long, noisy multi-session conversation histories; existing benchmarks/models emphasize explicit-fact retrieval, leaving open how well models can extract subtle, evolving preference signals rather than just recall long context.
mecanismo: PersonaMem-v2 dataset (1,000 personas, 20,000+ preferences, up to 128k-token multi-session histories) pairs with a MemAgent-inspired agentic-memory training approach: the conversation is split into fixed-size chunks and a single LLM iteratively updates a capped, human-readable memory M_i = f(C_i, M_{i-1}) under causality/Markovian/capped-size constraints, trained via GRPO reinforcement fine-tuning with verifiable MCQ rewards plus LLM-as-judge rewards for open-ended answers; the final query is answered from the last memory state M_T instead of the full transcript.
evaluacion: Frontier OpenAI models (GPT-5-Chat/mini/nano, GPT-4.1, o4-mini) benchmarked on 5,000 curated Q&A pairs (MCQ + open-ended, LLM-as-judge with 3x GPT-5-Chat instances); Qwen3-4B trained via SFT, GRPO, and the Agentic-Memory framework, compared against frontier baselines, with ablations isolating MCQ-only vs open-ended-only vs mixed reward training.
numeros_clave: Frontier LLMs 37-48% (abstract) / 40-55% (sec4.1.1) implicit-personalization accuracy; RFT'd Qwen3-4B reaches 53.8% MCQ / 56.0% open-ended vs GPT-5-Chat's 45.6%/46.2% (sec4.2.1); agentic-memory framework reaches SOTA 55% accuracy using a 2k-token memory vs 32k full history = 16x fewer input tokens (abstract, sec3.2); MCQ-only ablation collapses 13.1pp on open-ended, open-ended-only ablation drops 18.2pp on MCQ (sec4.2.2); preference-type breakdown: stereotypical 48.9+/-5.7% vs anti-stereotypical 33.0+/-5.0%, own-preference 42.1+/-4.9% vs other's-preference 17.5+/-11.7% (Fig.5).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Shortening context from 128k to 32k tokens (removing irrelevant conversation) gives NO significant accuracy improvement (sec4.1.2) -- a measured case where more/better retrieval context does not fix a reasoning bottleneck, cautioning MF against assuming better retrieval always helps.

The agentic-memory framework (sec3.2) sequentially distills chunks into a capped 2k-token human-readable memory that reaches SOTA 55% accuracy at 16x fewer tokens than full-history reasoning -- strong measured evidence that consolidating transient interaction history into a durable compact summary beats keeping everything.

The trained memory M_T is explicitly required to stay 'compact and human-readable' (sec3.2, capped-memory-size principle) and Fig.7 shows it as legible narrative prose, not embeddings -- direct support for MF's typed-narrative-docs-as-Tier-1 design over opaque vector stores.

The abstract's headline result is a 16x input-token reduction (2k memory vs 32k history) with a performance GAIN, not a trade-off -- the strongest context-economy number in this wave, directly on MF's COSTO anchor.

notes: sec4.1 (Fig.4/5) has frontier-LLM baseline numbers; sec4.2 (Fig.6/7) has the RL-trained Qwen3-4B and agentic-memory numbers; the 16x/2k-vs-32k figure recurs in abstract, sec1, and sec4.2.

cita: Murugesan, T. (2026). Enhancing SWE Bench with Context Engineering: A Comparative Study Against Prompt Engineering in LLM-Based Software Tasks.
problema: (As claimed) Prompt engineering alone plateaus on complex, multi-file SWE-Bench tasks that require repository history, architecture, and cross-file dependency understanding that cannot be encoded into an instruction alone.
mecanismo: (As claimed) A three-stage 'context engineering' preprocessing pipeline built atop SWE-agent: (1) repository traversal extracting code/historical/documentation/testing context, (2) hybrid heuristic+learned relevance scoring (weighted formula, dynamic threshold 0.65-0.75), (3) coherent hierarchical structuring -- injects roughly 900-1,200 extra tokens of repository context into the baseline SWE-Bench prompt (from ~175 to ~1,090+ tokens) before an LLM attempts the task, compared against baseline and prompt-engineered-only conditions.
evaluacion: Claims a controlled 3-condition (baseline / prompt-engineered / context-engineered) experiment on a stratified 240-task sample drawn from SWE-Bench's 2,294 issues, measuring task success, static-analysis quality metrics (maintainability, pattern-similarity), and AST-based hallucination detection; however, the paper's core quantitative claims (78% expert-alignment, 17-34% gains, 34-56% compute reduction, carbon-footprint figures) are attributed via citation to OTHER papers or blog posts ([3]-[6]), and no results table with per-model pass-rate numbers from this study's own executed run appears in the body.
numeros_clave: Claims (all attributed to external citations, not an own results table): prompt engineering alone <35% success on complex multi-file tasks; simple-task prompt-engineering gain +14% vs baseline; complex-task prompt-engineering gain only +4.2%; context-engineering gain +29.3% (up to >40% for some models) on complex debugging; relevance-scoring 78% expert-alignment (attributed to [3], an in-context-learning-for-codegen paper); compute reduction 34-56% and inference-cost reduction up to 47% (attributed to [5]/[6], a ResearchGate note and a company blog).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper claims a 'Documentation Context Extraction' stage pulls API references/inline comments (sec2.6) as one of four context sources, treating docs as a first-class input, but provides no traceable measurement isolating its contribution.

This paper's own headline numbers (78% expert-alignment, 17-34%/29.3% gains) are attributed to citations [3]-[6] that are either off-topic (an in-context-learning-for-codegen ACM paper) or non-peer-reviewed (a ResearchGate note, a company blog) rather than to a results table from ITS OWN described 240-task experiment -- a caution against treating cited 'measured retrieval' numbers at face value without checking the source.

The claimed token-flow accounting (baseline ~175 tokens to context-engineered ~1,090 tokens, sec2.6) is a concrete instance of the COSTO anchor's tokens-per-task concern, though its provenance (own measurement vs cited figure) is unclear.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: appears to be a template/AI-generated survey-style paper (single author, low-tier journal JISEM) -- its own 'Multi-Mode Experimental Harness' (sec2.3) and 240-task sample are described but no results table from THIS study's own run appears; all headline percentages are attributed via [3]-[6] to other, often unrelated or non-peer-reviewed sources; treat quantitative claims with caution.

cita: Logan (2026). Continuum Memory Architectures for Long-Horizon LLM Agents.
problema: RAG treats agent memory as a static, read-only lookup table: items persist unchanged, retrieval never modifies state, and temporal order is ignored, so agents cannot accumulate updated facts, connect events over time, or disambiguate context-dependent terms across long-horizon interactions.
mecanismo: The Continuum Memory Architecture (CMA) specifies memory as a graph-structured substrate (nodes=fragments with reinforcement/salience/timestamp/provenance, edges=semantic/temporal/associative) with an activation field that spreads graded activation per query; a lifecycle of ingest (salience/temporal-scope tagging, novelty-merge, capacity eviction), retrieval (multi-factor: vector similarity + activation + recency decay + structural reinforcement), mutation (retrieval reinforces accessed fragments, weakens near-misses), and background consolidation (replay strengthens temporal chains, abstraction extracts gists, episodic detail can fade into semantic knowledge).
evaluacion: A CMA instantiation (graph substrate + activation engine + retrieval scorer + consolidation jobs) is compared, via a GPT-4o LLM-judge protocol (blind A/B, 3 seeds, permutation and McNemar significance tests, p<0.01), against a Supabase-pgvector RAG baseline (with recency-weighted decay) using the SAME embeddings (text-embedding-3-small), across 4 behavioral probes: knowledge updates (40 queries/8 domains), temporal association (30 queries/10 episodes), associative recall (30 queries/5 project knowledge graphs), and disambiguation (48 queries/8 ambiguous terms).
numeros_clave: Table 1: CMA won 82/92 decisive trials overall (RAG 10, ties 39 excluded from decisive count); Knowledge Updates 38/40 CMA wins (Cohen's d=1.84); Temporal Association 13/14 decisive (Cohen's h=2.06, 47% both-wrong rate); Associative Recall 14/19 decisive (h=0.99); Disambiguation 17/20 decisive (h=1.55); permutation tests (10,000 shuffles) and McNemar's test both p<0.01 per study; latency cost: CMA mean 1.48s vs RAG 0.65s (about 2.4x slower).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: CMA's substrate is a graph of fragments with reinforcement/salience metadata, not a human-readable typed document (sec4) -- the opposite pole from MF's docs-as-truth premise, though its provenance/reinforcement fields could inform a doc-tier's staleness signals.

Study 3's 'project knowledge graphs' link people, milestones, and subsystems (sec5.3), treating project/plan structure as memory content, but CMA does not specialize a distinct plan-state layer the way MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor requires.

Table 1's measured 82/92 decisive wins (p<0.01, permutation+McNemar) show a graph+activation retrieval layer beating a strong recency-weighted RAG baseline on memory-dynamics tasks -- external evidence that vanilla similarity-only retrieval (closer to MF's current design) is measurably insufficient for update/temporal/associative queries.

The consolidation stage explicitly 'transforms streams of experience into reusable knowledge, allowing detailed episodes to fade once higher-level schemas emerge' (sec3/sec4) via replay and gist extraction -- a formalized promotion mechanism close to MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor.

notes: Table 1 (sec5.5) has per-probe win/tie counts and effect sizes; latency cost is sec5.5; single-author/self-built RAG baseline (Supabase pgvector) so treat magnitude with some caution, but stats (permutation+McNemar, p<0.01) are reported per study.

cita: Chrysochos (2026). Mind-Tool: Domain Memory Architecture for AI Agents.
problema: Stateless AI assistants (ChatGPT, Copilot) and even long-context-window agents lack persistent, structured domain knowledge, so every session 'starts with no grounded sense of where we are' -- for operational IT-infrastructure management (Proxmox/Kubernetes/networking) this forces constant re-explanation of system topology and repeated mistakes.
mecanismo: Mind-Tool maintains a Memory Folder of version-controlled markdown files (infra state, operational history, decision records, procedural runbooks) plus a 'Desired State' (conversational goal tracking) updated via natural dialogue rather than a batch initializer, and an AI Reasoning Engine (Claude Sonnet 4.5) that runs a continuous reconciliation loop -- read desired state vs memory folder, identify discrepancies, update memory files, execute actions through MCP-based tool servers (Proxmox/Kubernetes/GitLab/network APIs) -- deliberately using a single conversational agent (not a two-agent initializer+stateless-worker split) since a human is present to guard against context drift.
evaluacion: A 90-day (3-month) single-deployment production case study managing one operator's home-lab-scale infrastructure (Proxmox cluster, NAS, 2 VPS, planned k3s HA cluster), self-measuring task completion time, automation rate, success rate, and knowledge-file growth (Table 1), compared informally against a manual-baseline estimate and a 'stateless AI assistant' estimate -- no controlled trial, no other operators, no held-out ground-truth test set.
numeros_clave: 94% task success rate, 68% of requests automated, 62% time reduction (15 hours/week) vs manual baseline (Table 1); 147 markdown memory files / 8,437 lines after 90 days, average file age 45 days; automated completion 2.3 min vs human-assisted 8.7 min; 34 distinct workflows reused, 5.8 executions/procedure on average; claimed 85% time reduction vs manual and 73% vs a stateless-AI baseline (Fig.4, informal comparison, not a controlled experiment).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The Memory Folder is explicitly plain markdown, version-controlled via Git, human-readable by design -- a direct real-world instance of MF's Tier-1 typed-narrative-docs-as-truth premise, with self-reported production numbers (94% success) attached.

The 'Desired State' component is explicitly a persistent, dialogue-updated model of user goals compared against actual infrastructure state every reasoning cycle -- a working instance of plan-state-as-first-class-memory (MF's PLAN-ESTADO), reported to sustain 94% success over 90 days.

Fig.3's 'logarithmic growth pattern' is described as 'initial rapid learning followed by knowledge refinement and consolidation,' but the paper does not detail a concrete promotion/demotion mechanism, only an observed trend line.

Table 1's time-savings figures (62% reduction, 2.3min vs 8.7min per task) are the paper's central economic argument, directly on MF's COSTO anchor, though drawn from a single uncontrolled deployment rather than a comparative experiment.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: single-author, single-deployment (N=1 home-lab/small-VPS setup) case study in a journal (academicsquare-pub.com) that repeatedly frames itself as 'confirming/validating Anthropic's thesis' -- self-reported metrics (Table 1, Fig.3-5) have no control group or independent replication.

cita: Cros, A. & Ava (2026). .ava -- Une notation symbolique compressee pour la memoire persistante d'agents IA.
problema: LLM agents with persistent identities across sessions (e.g. 'Ava', 500+ sessions) accumulate memory files (MEMORY.md, SOUL.md) that grow too large to fit repeatedly in a finite context window (661 lines / roughly 8k tokens after 3 weeks); RAG, vector databases, and fine-tuning all treat memory as external to reasoning and none address the token DENSITY of the representation itself.
mecanismo: .ava is a hand-designed compact symbolic notation (positional grammar: category+name plus dot-attributes plus state marker, e.g. one glyph per domain such as infra, tools, project, person, a 'scar'/cicatrice symbol with severity 0-9, and an absolute-prohibition marker) achieving roughly 30x compression vs markdown on real memory files, paired with a 4-tier memory hierarchy (L1 active context window, L2 hot .ava-compressed memory plus a CURVATURE.md behavioral-bias profile loaded before facts, L3 warm semantic-embedding search, L4 cold uncompressed archive from which nothing is ever deleted); a Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct model is LoRA-fine-tuned (4-bit NF4, 6GB consumer GPU) across 5 dataset iterations to learn encoding/decoding the notation natively.
evaluacion: Compression measured directly on Ava's real memory files (Table 2: per-item ratios 5.4x-29.8x, roughly 30x on the full 661-line MEMORY.md); fine-tuning evaluated via token accuracy and loss across 5 training iterations (V1-V4b), with a held-out generalization check on novel infrastructure strings, best run V4b (444 balanced paraphrased examples, prompt/completion SFT loss, 3 epochs).
numeros_clave: Roughly 30x average compression on real MEMORY.md (about 24K chars to about 800 chars, Table 2); per-example compression 5.4x-29.8x; V4b fine-tune: loss 4.5 to 0.999, token accuracy 35.0% to 78.5% over 3 epochs (sec4.3.5); 3min14s / 168 steps / 4.33GB peak VRAM on a 6GB consumer GPU; V3 overfitting failure (5 epochs on 865 duplicated samples degrades vs V2); infra symbols about 45% of the training dataset vs identity symbols only about 12%, explaining systematic identity-symbol decode failures (sec4.4.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper explicitly rejects markdown-level readability as the target and optimizes for a terse symbolic notation instead (sec2.1-2.2) -- in tension with MF's premise that Tier-1 memory should be legible narrative prose; the L2 .ava/CURVATURE layer trades readability for 30x density.

The 4-layer hierarchy (sec3.5) keeps 'active projects' and CURVATURE.md state as part of L2 hot memory loaded every session, treating ongoing-work state as first-class, though the paper does not isolate plan-state from general facts.

Sec3.4's explicit design principle states the AI should NOT imitate human forgetting -- 'keep everything (full archive) while developing curvature' -- directly opposing memory-economy-through-forgetting strategies MF's NEGATIVO anchor might favor.

The measured roughly-30x token-density gain (Table 2) on real memory files is a concrete, quantified lossy-compression lever for context economy that MF could evaluate as an alternative/complement to summarization-based compaction.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: self-published (Avalon Research, single independent author plus an AI-agent co-author 'Ava'), no peer review, personal-project scale (N=1 agent's memory files, 6GB consumer GPU); Table 2 (sec2.5) has compression ratios, sec4.3.5 has the V4b loss/accuracy curve, Table 3 (sec4.5) compares all 5 fine-tuning versions.

cita: Liu et al. (2026). Semantic XPath: Structured Agentic Memory Access for Conversational AI.
problema: Conversational AI agents doing long-term, task-oriented interactions (itinerary planning, to-do lists, meal plans) need structured memory that preserves hierarchical task organization and revision history; in-context memory scales poorly (fails half of requests after only five turns) and flat-RAG ignores the natural tree structure, retrieving items from the wrong branch (e.g. the wrong day of a trip).
mecanismo: SemanticXPath represents conversational memory as a typed, rooted tree (schema-derived node types plus attributes, e.g. Itinerary->Version->Day->POI) and defines an XPath-style query grammar (axis navigator / and //; node selector; positional selector [i]; a semantic-relevance operator combining local embedding-similarity or NLI-entailment scores with aggregation avg/min/max/gmean and boolean-like composition 1-P, P1 op P2) executed by a single recursive weighted-node-set evaluation function, retrieving/updating only the relevant substructure and versioning updates as new branches.
evaluacion: Compared against in-context memory and flat-RAG baselines (GPT-5-mini and Gemini-3-flash backbones, Qwen3-Embedding-8B for flat RAG) across 3 ConvAI domains (travel itinerary, to-do list, meal-kit recommendation), each with 20 single-turn plus 5 multi-turn curated conversations, measuring average pass rate and token usage (RQ1 single-turn, RQ2 multi-turn with growing history).
numeros_clave: Abstract: SemanticXPath improves pass rate 176.7% over flat-RAG while using only 9.1% of in-context tokens; single-turn (Fig.5): pass rates about 79-83% (SemanticXPath) vs about 70-80% (in-context) vs about 27-38% (flat RAG), in-context token usage about 5x higher than SemanticXPath/flat-RAG (about 26-69k vs about 3.2-5.9k tokens); multi-turn (Fig.6/7): SemanticXPath maintains stable token usage across 7 turns while in-context grows steadily, and in-context pass rate drops on multi-turn history-dependent requests while SemanticXPath stays close to single-turn levels.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: SemanticXPath's schema-derived compositional tree (Itinerary->Version->Day->POI, sec3.1) with explicit Version nodes for revision history is a concrete typed-structure pattern MF could adopt to organize Tier-1 docs by task hierarchy rather than flat prose.

The to-do-list domain (Fig.4) models tasks with 'progress status, priority level, and deadline' as first-class tree attributes updated through interaction, treating this evolving task state as 'the agent's current working state' -- directly measuring plan-state-as-memory value (176.7% pass-rate gain).

Flat-RAG (semantic-similarity-only retrieval, closer to MF's ADR-019 baseline) scores only about 27-38% pass rate vs SemanticXPath's about 79-83% (Fig.5) on the SAME embedding model -- direct measured evidence that structure-blind retrieval is insufficient once memory has hierarchy.

Fig.7 shows in-context token usage growing unboundedly with turn count while SemanticXPath's stays flat -- direct, well-isolated evidence that structured retrieval (not just any RAG) is what keeps context economy sub-linear in conversation length.

notes: Fig.5 (single-turn pass-rate/tokens) and Fig.6/7 (multi-turn) are the core result figures; Appendix A has the full formal query-execution semantics; the abstract's 176.7%/9.1% headline numbers are aggregated across all 3 domains.
